rates.status: MEASURED CO-RUN. T_G co-run = 0.1474 s/block (median of 25 base-block samples, 99.8% of GPU-time overlapping NPU executes; same-session solo 0.1600); T_N co-run = 0.6484 s/block (9 GEMMs at 0.3904 under GPU load + 0.2580 downsep). T_N/T_G = 4.40. T_V is now COMPLETE in all three configurations (convs + mid-block attention measured on both engines): 10.640 s hybrid, 11.155 all-TPU, 12.342 all-Mali. k_b* = 160 on the hybrid, and the locked 160 survives iff the attention runs on Mali (on the TPU it is 161, +0.6% period). Sustained-run check PASSES (tools/npu/sustain_npu.py, capture sustain_npu_20261115_214149, docs/device/RESULTS_sustain_npu.md): 60 rounds x 9 GEMMs = 24.6 s of continuous TPU work, drift +0.35% (first-20% 408.902 ms vs last-20% 410.346 ms per round; slope +0.03 ms/round; TPU zone 25.0 -> 31.0 C) => no throttling over a full NPU stage, so T_N needs no derating term. Still TBD: ffn.down under contention (0.2580 s is solo - corun holds only the 9 block GEMMs), and the decode's CONV_2D class (10.554 s) was not soaked for 23.5 s. Per-tensor-scale parity is MEASURED (2.15x mean GEMM error, 6/40 Gate-1 cosine failures) - see gate_4_parity and docs/device/RESULTS_scales.md.
rates.note: must be measured with both engines co-running, at the target resolution and thermal state; report the solo number as a kernel rate only

rates.T_N_hybrid_note: 0.4178 (9/10 on the TPU, gate-compliant capture) + 0.04733 (ffn.down on Mali, MEASURED) = 0.4651 s/block -> T_N/T_G = 2.87. Use THIS T_N if ffn.down lands on Mali, which is the engineering recommendation; the 0.6758 / 4.18x figure above is the all-TPU architecture. Solving the cut with the wrong one moves k_b*.
rates.T_V_conv_tpu_status: COMPLETE gate-compliant measured sum over 100% of the decode conv MACs, as kT shifted 2-D CONV_2D taps, one execute per frame per tap (batch>1 will not compile above ~1 MB/frame). Sweep start TPU 32.0 C vs a 32.1 C battery+3 gate (PASS, confirmed on a second sample); the two dominant classes (68% of MACs) ran at that floor. T_V_s_per_chunk is now SET: the mid-block 3-D attention was subsequently measured (32.38 GMAC: 0.601 s on the TPU vs 0.0855 s on Mali, 7.0x), so the decode is complete in all three configurations (10.640 hybrid / 11.155 all-TPU / 12.342 all-Mali). Hot control run (18:17): 11.412 s -> the cool run is 7.5% faster. Evidence: docs/device/RESULTS_vae_tv.md, conv_sweep_20261115_182512.json, attn_tv_20261115_211944.json.
rates.T_V_conv_tpu_note: CONV_2D reaches 719-2024 GOPS on this HAL on the gate-compliant run (685-1842 on the hot control) vs 285 GOPS for FULLY_CONNECTED: the Edge TPU is a conv engine and the DiT block's 10 GEMMs are being served by the wrong op class. Worth testing ffn.up/attn as 1x1 CONV_2D before accepting the 4.18x T_N/T_G penalty as silicon.
rates.T_V_engine_convention_note: The GOPS columns in RESULTS_vae_tv.md are NOT on the same basis. The TPU numbers (969.7 aggregate, 2024 best class) are FLOP/s = 2xMAC/s. The Mali class column (378-486) and its 417.5 aggregate are MAC/s. Like-for-like Mali is 835.1 FLOP-GOPS, so the TPU is 1.161x faster at the decode - identical to the time ratio 12.256/10.554, which is the number to quote. On that basis the Mali conv kernel runs at 95.2% of Mali's own 877 FLOP-GOPS GEMM rate (47.2% of the 1770 peak), NOT the '48% of the GEMM rate' stated in RESULTS_vae_tv.md section 6 - 48% looks like percent-of-peak. Consequence: the 'halo-staged activation tile, 871 GOPS ceiling' next action assumes ~2x headroom that this arithmetic does not support; residual headroom is ~5% aggregate, ~14% on the best class.

cut.formula: period(k_b) = max(k_b*T_G, (B-k_b)*T_N + T_V); k* = (B*T_N + T_V)/(T_N + T_G)
cut.B_note: 6 denoising steps x 30 DiT blocks per 9-frame chunk (docs/00_START_HERE.md, docs/02_model_spec.md). The formula needs B and it existed only in prose.
cut.k_b_solo_estimate_note: Solo-rate cross-check of the solved k_b=160 (not the number of record). With B=180, T_G=0.1618, T_V=10.554 and all-TPU T_N=0.6758: k* = 157.8 blocks (87.7% on Mali), both sides balance at 25.54 s against 39.68 s for all-180-blocks-plus-decode serial on Mali -> 1.55x. With the hybrid T_N=0.4651 (ffn.down on Mali): k* = 150.4 (83.5%), period 24.33 s, 1.63x. The co-run pair supersedes this; the two agree within 1.3% on k_b.
cut.next_measurement_priority: Sustained throttling is RETIRED for the cool regime: a 60-round / 24.6 s continuous soak (tools/npu/sustain_npu.py) drifted +0.35% (first-20% 408.902 ms vs last-20% 410.346 ms per round, slope +0.03 ms/round) with the TPU zone at 25.0 -> 31.0 C, so T_N carries no derating term. What remains: (a) ffn.down (0.2580 of the 0.6484) is still solo - corun holds only the 9 block GEMMs; (b) the decode's CONV_2D class (10.554 s) was not soaked; (c) the soak topped out at 31 C whereas the same GEMM workload has been measured heating TPU 29 -> 59 C in 54 s, so a warm 200-chunk pipeline (P3.1) can still reach a regime no soak has covered. Off the rate path entirely: Gate 1's PSNR/SSIM leg is runnable now (.venv-ref, torch 2.15.0+cpu), which also arms Gate 4's frame parity.
cut.status: SOLVED from co-run rates: k_b = 160 (GPU blocks [0,160), NPU [160,180) then the decode), period 23.61 s = max(23.58 GPU, 23.61 NPU) with the hybrid T_V = 10.640, idle 0.02 s, 5.394x against NPU-only (127.35 s). Cross-check with the conservative solo pair (T_G 0.1618, T_N 0.6758): k* = 157.8, period 25.54 s, i.e. the two agree within 1.3% on k_b. Sensitivity: step-level granularity (k_b multiple of L=30) forces k_b=150 and costs 27.3%; ignoring T_V when solving puts k_b at 147 and costs 36.5% once the decode is paid serially. T_V is complete in all three engine splits and the 24.6 s soak showed no derating, so the only open item above this number is ffn.down measured solo rather than under contention.

phase3_pipeline._comment: Build order: phase3_pipeline/PLAN.md. P3.1 measured 2026-11-15 22:03 -> docs/device/RESULTS_handoff_p31.md
phase3_pipeline.p3_1_handoff: PASS - two-process MAP_SHARED two-slot ring, 200 chunks: 0 mismatching words of 587,520/chunk, 200/200 in order, t_cons > t_prod on 400/400 publishes. Ring file 9,408,512 B = PAGE (4096-B header page: seq/done per slot) + 2 x SLOT_STRIDE (4,702,208 = 4,700,160 payload rounded up to a page) - exactly two slots, which a third buffer would have exposed as a size mismatch. Split --role producer / --role consumer from two separate adb sessions passed 30/30 with stream_done=1 - the shape P3.2/P3.3 will use.
phase3_pipeline.p3_1_latency: publish->consume 680.9 us mean / 661.7 median / 1023 max free-running; 2541.4 mean / 8167 max with a 1 ms consumer stall. msync(4 KiB, MS_SYNC) median 63.7 us (mean 88.9) = 0.0004% of a 23.61 s chunk, so the pessimistic barrier is affordable and there is no case for MS_ASYNC.
phase3_pipeline.p3_1_decision_input: Back-pressure is the NORMAL path: the producer blocked on 198/200 chunks even free-running, because writing 4.7 MB costs ~0.15 ms while the consumer's verify pass costs ~0.6 ms. So the second slot is required, not an optimisation - a one-slot ring serialises the test into 200 x (write + read).
phase3_pipeline.payload_tokens_note: The ring carries M = 1530 tokens (3 latent frames x 510) x d 1536 in fp16 = 4,700,160 B = 4.48 MiB. T_G was measured at exactly M=1530, and T_N's 4 x 384 = 1536 token tiles cover 1530 with padding, so the solved rates apply to the real chunk without a token-count correction.
phase3_pipeline.p3_1_not_established: No period, overlap or CPU-time split (P3.4/P3.5); nothing about the INT8 weight artifact (the ring carries the fp16 residual for the test); one-slot starvation behaviour unmeasured. Correctness test only - thermal was recorded (TPU 25.0 -> 25.0 C, battery 21.8 -> 21.8 C), not gated.
phase3_pipeline.p3_2_gpu_stage: PASS on correctness, with a 32% cost that is now a DECISION, not a detail (docs/device/RESULTS_proc_a_p32.md, commits fc15363/9f52635). Same binary, real artifacts/blocks/block_00.bin, 8 blocks per route: route B (file mmap + clImportMemoryARM) gives 10/10 weights zero-copy, 80/80 GEMMs, 8/8 chunks drained by a second PID.
phase3_pipeline.p3_2_zero_copy_cost: ZERO-COPY IS NOT FREE ON THE GPU STAGE: import 214.5 ms/block (661.9 GOPS) vs device-local staging 162.2 ms/block (875.4 GOPS, reproducing the 161.8 ms benchmark). +32.2%. The penalty tracks the weight working set - both FFN planes (13.8 MB each) go +15/+16%, attention only +4% - so it is per-byte cost, not per-import overhead.
phase3_pipeline.p3_2_cut_consequence_not_applied: k_b* 157 with period 25.55 s (staging) / k_b* 148 with period 31.75 s (import), against the locked 160 / 23.61 s. Reported, NOT applied: k_b stays 160 until the one-copy-vs-speed decision below is taken.
phase3_pipeline.p3_2_open_decision: ONE INT8 COPY vs GPU SPEED. The project premise is a single copy shared by both engines; zero-copy import costs 32% of the GPU stage, and staging to device-local memory recovers it only by making a second copy. Both branches are measured (25.55 s vs 31.75 s period), so this is now the student's call. UNTESTED HYPOTHESIS worth one experiment first: on a unified-memory SoC the Mali GPU and the CPU share the same LPDDR4X, so a 32% per-byte penalty is more consistent with a cache-attribute/mapping effect in clImportMemoryARM (uncached or write-through mapping) than with bandwidth physics - the working-set scaling fits that reading. Route A (AHardwareBuffer, which Gate 2 verified also imports) and/or different import hints are the cheap tests; if either recovers the 32%, the one-copy premise survives at full speed.
phase3_pipeline.p3_2_not_in_any_period_yet: Host-side payload conversion costs 44-57 ms/block and is NOT in either period above; it is removable with an fp16 epilogue kernel, so no corrected period is quoted until that exists. Attention/softmax/AdaLN are still outside the stage. Both runs started 0.3-0.9 C over the battery+3 line on the idle floor (floor-grade, recorded).

npu_constraints.reduction_dim_note: one FULLY_CONNECTED [N=1536,K] compiles at K=1280/1536/1600/1664 (0.34-0.52 s) and fails OP_FAILED from K=1792 up (46-59 s; K=8960 also gave DEAD_OBJECT after 62 s). ffn.up - the same 13.7 MB of weights at K=1536 - compiles in 1.44 s, so the ceiling is the reduction dim, not N or weight bytes. The support query reports every one of those shapes 'supported', so it is not a viability test. Chunk to <=1664, one compilation per op (ffn.down = 7x FC[1536,1280] + 6x ADD, 2.57 s total); chunking inside a single graph does NOT work (down2 = 2x K=4480 + ADD, all ops supported, compile OP_FAILED at 47.8 s).
npu_constraints.graph_shape: one graph per (block, token-tile); whole-block graphs validated and were SUPPORTED by google-edgetpu but Compilation_finish REBOOTED THE DEVICE (2026-11-15) -> one graph per GEMM is the only viable path
npu_constraints.weight_scales: per-tensor only: TENSOR_QUANT8_SYMM_PER_CHANNEL is rejected by FULLY_CONNECTED with addOperation BAD_DATA(4), so the per-output-column scheme cannot be expressed on the NPU stage. DECISION PENDING, but no longer a guess - the cost is measured on the real checkpoint (docs/device/RESULTS_scales.md, 40 GEMM instances = blocks 0/5/15/29 x 10): per-tensor costs 2.15x the mean GEMM output error (3.01% vs 1.40%; median-of-ratios 1.74x, worst 5.44x) and breaks the Gate-1 cosine>=0.999 bar on 6/40 outputs (worst 0.996820), where per-column breaks 0/40 (min 0.999926). The penalty is a WEIGHT property, not a shape property: it tracks per-column scale spread at r=0.805 (per-column error vs spread r=0.101), so a shape-based restriction is unsupportable; the only defensible restriction is per-tensor-where-cheap, attn2.to_k + attn2.to_v = 10.2% of block MACs, leaving 89.8% of block MACs unable to use the NPU under the locked quantisation.
npu_constraints.uncompilable_shape: FC with K=8960 (ffn.down) -> OP_FAILED at 47.2 s / DEAD_OBJECT at 62.0 s, reproduced in fresh processes; it is the K>1664 ceiling, not this shape (see reduction_dim_ceiling). Both workarounds are now MEASURED: chunked 7x FC[1536,1280] + 6x ADD on the TPU = 0.2580 s/block (163.9 GOPS); Mali tiled = 0.04733 s/block (893 GOPS) -> the TPU is 5.45x slower for this GEMM. Engineering recommendation: ffn.down on Mali whichever way the cut lands; the decision is the student's
npu_constraints.conv2d_batch_ceiling: CONV_2D compiles with a batch dim only while the per-frame input is small: N=3 at 0.78 MB/frame compiles in 141.6 ms; N=5/N=3 at 1.4 MB/frame and N=3/N=9 at 6.3 MB/frame grind 31-36 s in Compilation_finish and fail, while the same 37.6 MB tensor compiles in 263 ms at N=1. getSupportedOperationsForDevices reports these shapes delegated=1 and is again not a viability test. Decompose on the frame axis: one execute per frame per temporal tap.
